signature: discover_and_prove(expr: str, fn: Callable[[int], int], check_upto: int = 60, judge_timeout_ms: int = 2500) -> ArithmeticFinding
requires: expr denotes a univariate integer polynomial in n accepted by the existing exact kernel bridge and fn computes that same polynomial over integer inputs.
check_upto and judge_timeout_ms retain their existing positive bounded meanings; callers do not interpret a bounded refutation sweep alone as a universal proof.
The immutable legacy baseline and committed discovery SAMPLE-REPORT remain available as differential oracles.
ensures: The exact polynomial degree selects the proof portfolio before any timing-sensitive solver call: degree four or greater uses complete residue exhaustion directly, while degree three or less retains the legacy induction and CRT-first path with residue exhaustion as its honest fallback.

The canonical seven-polynomial discovery family emits induction for the two degree-two laws, modulus-factoring for the two degree-three laws, and residue-exhaustion for the three degree-four-or-greater laws on every supported OS and Python version.
A degree-four-or-greater canonical law never changes certainty, method, reason, proof hash, or rendered report bytes because a solver happened to finish before a wall-clock timeout on one host.
Every proved finding remains independently checked and kernel verified; deterministic strategy selection never upgrades an empirical survivor or solver timeout into a proof.
The committed discovery SAMPLE-REPORT is byte-identical to a fresh render on every supported matrix cell.
raises: Inputs outside the required integer-polynomial domain retain the existing kernel, parser, or arithmetic error boundary rather than receiving a fabricated finding.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, and interpreter defects are not converted into proof outcomes.
A failed independent or kernel check cannot be represented as independently_verified or kernel_verified.

effects.process: none beyond the already-declared in-process solver calls on the degree-three-or-less legacy path
effects.cache: the caller-owned run_arithmetic_discovery cache may retain the returned immutable-by-convention findings; strategy selection itself has no cache
effects.mutation: does not mutate expr, fn, contracts, generated reports, tracker records, or the immutable legacy baseline

determinism.degree: len(poly_from_sympy(expr)) minus one after exact canonical coefficient normalization
determinism.high_degree: degree at least four always selects residue-exhaustion before a solver call
determinism.canonical_methods: induction, induction, residue-exhaustion, induction, modulus-factoring, residue-exhaustion, residue-exhaustion in POLY_FAMILY order
determinism.report: method and certainty selection excludes elapsed time, host speed, architecture, checkout path, and solver scheduling

budget.refutation: at most check_upto plus one exact fn evaluations before proof selection
budget.high_degree: at most modulus exact residue evaluations and zero induction solver calls
budget.low_degree: existing bounded induction calls use judge_timeout_ms per prime-power part before the complete residue fallback
budget.memory: bounded by the canonical polynomial coefficients, prime-power list, and at most modulus residue results

epistemics.proved: a complete universal proof was independently checked and a kernel proof term was successfully minted
epistemics.refuted: an exact integer input violates the proposed divisibility claim
epistemics.unknown: the selected bounded proof path did not establish the claim and no complete fallback established it
epistemics.method: names the deterministic selected proof strategy, not whichever timing-sensitive backend returned first

invariants: No wall-clock race or solver timeout changes the canonical discovery report.
No strategy label claims stronger evidence than the proof actually checked.
The seven canonical proof hashes and their axiom lists remain content-addressed and unchanged.
No test, supported matrix cell, profile command, or coverage threshold is removed or weakened.
Accepted contracts and frozen legacy evidence remain byte-identical.
